title: Submit a ticket — regrouped, review step redesigned (round 1)

steps.path: Settings → Help & feedback → Report a bug
steps.headline: Writing a ticket: Bug or Feature comes first, and every note sits inside the card it is about.
steps.changed: The Bug/Feature switch moved to the top of the card. The tiny "tickets are public" line moved to the card's foot. The files note moved inside the "Include with ticket" card.
steps.notice: Same fields and tick boxes. When the button is grey, the card's last line also says why ("Add a title and a description to carry on").

steps.path: Report a bug → fill it in → Review ticket
steps.headline: The review step now shows your ticket as it will read, then everything that goes with it, in one card.
steps.changed: Before, review showed the same editable boxes again (and Bug/Feature vanished). Now: your title with a Bug or Feature pill, your description, then a "Sent with it" card holding the version line and the logs.
steps.notice: To change the words you press Back to draft — the review step is for reading. The logs box can still be edited here.

steps.path: Report a bug → Review ticket, with logs ticked
steps.headline: How should the review step show what will be sent? Pick one.

variants.label: Everything shown
variants.summary: Each attached piece is shown in full under "Sent with it". Longest, but nothing is hidden.

variants.label: Folded rows
variants.summary: Each piece is one row with a short summary ("4 lines"); click to read or edit it. Shortest, but you must open a row to see what is sent.

variants.label: One page
variants.summary: No review step: ticking a box shows what it adds right under it, and Submit is on the same page. Fewer clicks; the page gets long, and AI help moves onto it.

steps.headline: Optional AI help: each action is one row — what it does on the left, its button on the right.
steps.changed: Two wide outlined buttons and a tiny warning line under the second became two rows: "Improve the wording" with Rewrite, and "Let your assistant try to fix it" with Start, each explained in a line.
steps.notice: Still folded until you open it, and still only on the review step.

steps.headline: Back to draft and Submit now sit side by side at the right, Submit on the right, like other wide popups.
steps.changed: They were two full-width buttons stacked, Submit on top. The design guide puts a pair side by side in a wide popup; this popup is wide.
steps.notice: At phone width they still stack full width, Submit on top. This reverses an older sign-off ("Submit with Back to draft beneath it").

steps.headline: When sending fails, one red box replaces the buttons: what GitHub said, with Back to draft and Try again inside it.
steps.changed: Before: a grey box at the top with a bold title, a centred Retry, and the Submit button gone from the bottom. Now the notice sits where the buttons were, with no title and no guessed cause.
steps.notice: Your words are untouched; Try again sends the same ticket again.

steps.path: Review ticket → Submit with no network
steps.headline: With no network, the box says so in plain words instead of "getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND api.github.com".
steps.changed: Shown only when the computer itself reports no network connection (the same rule as Games). Amber, like Games' no-internet box.
steps.notice: Any other failure still shows GitHub's own words, as in the slide before.

steps.path: AI help → Let your assistant try to fix it → setup fails
steps.headline: If the assistant can't set up a working copy, it now says that — not "Your ticket wasn't sent".
steps.changed: Before, this failure was headed "Your ticket wasn't sent" and its Retry sent the ticket. Now it names the setup failure, and Try again retries the setup.
steps.notice: Nothing is sent to GitHub by this action, so the box says your ticket was not sent.

steps.headline: After sending, the result sits in one card, with Done and Open my ticket side by side.
steps.changed: The two sentences and two stacked buttons were loose on the popup. Now one card; Open my ticket (filled) on the right.

steps.path: Tick Screenshots or files → Continue in GitHub
steps.headline: Finishing in GitHub: the same one card, Open it again and Done side by side.
steps.changed: Done was filled under an outlined button; it is now on the right, the filled side, in a card.
steps.notice: Same words, including the note when the link had to drop part of the ticket.

steps.path: Submit public ticket, while it sends
steps.headline: "Sending your ticket…" now sits in a card instead of floating in the middle of the popup.
steps.changed: The spinner line moved into a card at the top, left-aligned.
steps.notice: It only shows for a moment.

steps.path: AI help → Let your assistant try to fix it
steps.headline: Setting up a working copy: the spinner and its note share one card.
steps.changed: The centred spinner and the loose note under it are now one card.

steps.path: AI help → Let your assistant try to fix it → done
steps.headline: "Your assistant is on it": one card with its Done button.
steps.changed: Same words and button, now in a card.

steps.headline: Reporting from an error now starts with "This happened in Office." — it was supposed to, but never did.
steps.changed: A bug: the popup was ready before the error happened, so the starting line and the Diagnose shortcut never arrived. Both work now.
steps.notice: Diagnose with the assistant now opens on the review step with AI help open, as it promised. Words you already typed are never replaced.

steps.path: Phone: Report a bug → Review ticket
steps.headline: On a phone the review step uses the same cards, and the two buttons stack full width.
steps.changed: Same as the desktop review step, narrower.
steps.notice: Submit is on top when stacked.

steps.path: Include with ticket → Error details and version
steps.headline: Should unticking "Error details and version" also stop the app version and computer type being added?
steps.today: Every bug ticket ends with a line like "YouCoded v1.3.0 · desktop · linux 7.1", added when it is sent, even when "Error details and version" is unticked.
steps.problem: Unticking the box suggests the version is left out, but the version and the computer's system name are still sent. Nothing on screen shows that line.
steps.proposal: Pick what should happen. Nothing has been changed yet; what is sent today is exactly as before.

options.label: Untick removes it
pros: The tick box means what it says
Nothing about your computer goes out unless you chose it
cons: Tickets without a version are harder for maintainers to act on

options.label: Always send, but show it
pros: The review step lists the line, so nothing is hidden
cons: The tick box then only controls the error text, and needs a new name

options.label: Leave as is
cons: The screen keeps saying less than what is sent
